summary: 71-year-old male on Day 6 post-left M1 ischemic stroke (s/p tenecteplase and TICI 2b thrombectomy; stable NIHSS 9 with Broca aphasia and right hemiparesis) who developed acute fever (38.4 C), sinus tachycardia (112 bpm), tachypnea (24 breaths/min), and hypoxemia (SpO2 89% on room air, 94% on 3 L/min NC) three hours after inadvertent thin-liquid oral intake despite failed bedside dysphagia screening and NPO status. Chest radiograph shows new right lower lobe consolidation with WBC 14.8 x10^9/L, CRP 96 mg/L, and procalcitonin 0.85 ng/mL. Requires prompt empiric aspiration pneumonia antibiotics, strict NPO enforcement, and secured enteral access for nutrition and held atorvastatin 80 mg.
suggested_differentials: Aspiration pneumonia
Hospital-acquired pneumonia
Acute pulmonary embolism
detected_red_flags: Acute hypoxemia (SpO2 89% on room air) with tachypnea (RR 24 breaths/min) and tachycardia (HR 112 bpm)
Fever (38.4 C), leukocytosis (WBC 14.8 x10^9/L), elevated procalcitonin, and new right lower lobe consolidation
Thin-liquid oral intake violating NPO precautions after failed dysphagia screen with pooled secretions
Delayed empiric antimicrobial therapy and absence of enteral access for nutrition and secondary prevention medications

summary: 58-year-old female on Postoperative Day 2 after right frontotemporal craniotomy for glioblastoma with acute neurological decline from GCS 15 to GCS 10 (E2V3M5), new right-sided anisocoria (5 mm sluggish vs 3 mm brisk), left upper extremity weakness (3/5), hypertension (184/98 mmHg), bradycardia (52 bpm), and irregular bradypnea (11 breaths/min). Currently maintained on dexamethasone 10 mg IV q6h, levetiracetam 1000 mg IV q12h, and 3% hypertonic saline infusion with stable serum sodium of 138 mmol/L. STAT repeat head CT and emergent neurosurgical intervention are warranted for suspected postoperative mass effect.
suggested_differentials: Postoperative epidural or resection-cavity hematoma
Malignant postoperative cerebral edema with early uncal herniation
Non-convulsive status epilepticus
detected_red_flags: Acute GCS decline from 15 to 10 with new right-sided anisocoria and contralateral left hemiparesis
Cushing triad physiology (BP 184/98 mmHg, HR 52 bpm, irregular RR 11 breaths/min)

summary: 66-year-old female with GOLD Stage IV COPD admitted for infective exacerbation now presenting with progressive somnolence (GCS 13), asterixis, tachypnea (28 breaths/min) with accessory muscle recruitment, and acute-on-chronic respiratory acidosis (pH 7.24, PaCO2 78 mmHg, HCO3 32 mmol/L). Oxygenation is currently well maintained at SpO2 97% on 6 L/min simple face mask, and chest radiograph shows hyperinflation without focal consolidation. Continue nebulized albuterol/ipratropium, IV methylprednisolone 40 mg daily, and azithromycin, and initiate noninvasive ventilation (BiPAP).
suggested_differentials: Acute-on-chronic hypercapnic respiratory failure due to COPD exacerbation
Acute decompensated heart failure
detected_red_flags: Severe uncompensated respiratory acidosis (pH 7.24, PaCO2 78 mmHg) with hypercapnic encephalopathy and asterixis
Respiratory muscle fatigue with accessory muscle recruitment and paradoxical abdominal motion

summary: 34-year-old male five weeks post-C5 AIS A complete tetraplegia presenting during occupational therapy with severe paroxysmal hypertension (198/114 mmHg vs baseline 96/58 mmHg), reflex bradycardia (46 bpm), pounding occipital headache, blurred vision, and supralesional diaphoresis and flushing. Examination reveals palpable bladder distension secondary to a kinked 16 Fr Foley catheter with four hours of anuria plus four days without bowel movement. Requires immediate upright positioning, catheter unkinking/bladder decompression, fecal impaction evaluation, immediate hold of scheduled midodrine 5 mg PO TID, and rapid-acting antihypertensive therapy if hypertension persists.
suggested_differentials: Autonomic dysreflexia secondary to acute urinary retention and possible fecal impaction
Intracerebral hemorrhage or hypertensive encephalopathy
Acute urosepsis with neurogenic bladder dysfunction
detected_red_flags: Autonomic dysreflexia crisis (BP 198/114 mmHg, >100 mmHg above baseline, HR 46 bpm, severe headache, visual blurring)
Acute urinary retention from kinked Foley catheter with 4 hours of anuria and palpable bladder distension
Four-day obstipation representing potential fecal impaction trigger
Active standing order for midodrine 5 mg PO TID contraindicated during hypertensive crisis

summary: 52-year-old male on Hospital Day 21 with severe Guillain-Barre syndrome and tracheostomy who failed a pressure-support weaning trial at 45 minutes with rapid shallow breathing (RR 34 breaths/min, RSBI 136), acute respiratory acidosis (pH 7.32, PaCO2 52 mmHg), SpO2 91% on FiO2 0.30, and left lower lobe atelectasis. Telemetry shows severe dysautonomia with BP swings (84/50 to 192/106 mmHg) and two 2.8-second sinus pauses after suctioning. Bedside mechanics remain borderline with FVC 21 mL/kg and NIF -32 cmH2O while completing Day 2 of intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG). Return to full ventilatory support, intensify airway clearance, and discontinue metoprolol tartrate 25 mg BID immediately.
suggested_differentials: Neuromuscular respiratory muscle fatigue and weaning failure in Guillain-Barre syndrome
Severe GBS-associated cardiovascular dysautonomia
Mucus plugging with lobar atelectasis or early ventilator-associated pneumonia
detected_red_flags: Severe cardiovascular dysautonomia with labile BP (84/50 to 192/106 mmHg) and 2.8-second sinus pauses
Ventilator weaning failure with RSBI 136 and acute respiratory acidosis (pH 7.32, PaCO2 52 mmHg)
Impaired airway clearance (peak cough flow 120 L/min) with new left lower lobe atelectasis
Scheduled metoprolol tartrate 25 mg BID posing high risk of severe bradyarrhythmia or asystole

summary: 54-year-old female on Post-Bleed Day 7 after ruptured anterior communicating artery aneurysm (Hunt-Hess 3, modified Fisher 4, s/p coiling and right frontal EVD) presenting with acute neurological deterioration (GCS 14 to 12, new abulia, right lower extremity weakness 3/5) following a post-nimodipine blood pressure drop from 158/86 to 114/64 mmHg (MAP 81 mmHg). TCD confirms severe vasospasm (left ACA MFV 168 cm/s, left MCA MFV 196 cm/s, Lindegaard ratio 4.6). Labs show hypovolemic hyponatremia (Na 127 mmol/L, urine Na 118 mmol/L, 24-hour fluid balance -1.4 L) indicative of cerebral salt wasting. Requires emergent induced hypertension, isotonic/hypertonic volume repletion, and urgent neurointerventional evaluation.
suggested_differentials: Delayed cerebral ischemia secondary to severe cerebral vasospasm
Cerebral salt wasting causing symptomatic hypovolemic hyponatremia
EVD-associated ventriculitis or acute hydrocephalus
detected_red_flags: Acute focal neurological decline on Post-Bleed Day 7 (GCS 14 to 12, abulia, right leg paresis 3/5)
Severe cerebral vasospasm on TCD (left ACA MFV 168 cm/s, left MCA MFV 196 cm/s, Lindegaard ratio 4.6)
Post-nimodipine systemic hypotension (114/64 mmHg, MAP 81 mmHg) impairing cerebral perfusion pressure
Severe hypovolemic hyponatremia (Na 127 mmol/L, fluid balance -1.4 L, urine Na 118 mmol/L) consistent with cerebral salt wasting

summary: 27-year-old male on Day 24 post-severe TBI with diffuse axonal injury who developed recurrent hyperthermia (39.6 C), tachycardia (148 bpm), hypertension (178/104 mmHg), tachypnea (34 breaths/min), and extensor posturing triggered by nursing stimuli, now complicated by persistent generalized lead-pipe rigidity and GCS decline from 11 to 9 after receiving haloperidol 5 mg IM twice in 12 hours. Labs confirm acute rhabdomyolysis (CK 4,850 U/L, dipstick-positive myoglobinuria), acute kidney injury (creatinine 1.4 mg/dL, potassium 5.1 mmol/L), and lactate 3.2 mmol/L. Requires immediate ICU transfer, strict discontinuation of haloperidol, aggressive IV crystalloid resuscitation, active cooling, and targeted PSH/NMS therapy.
suggested_differentials: Paroxysmal sympathetic hyperactivity secondary to severe traumatic brain injury
Neuroleptic malignant syndrome precipitated by haloperidol exposure
Systemic sepsis or occult central nervous system infection
detected_red_flags: Severe hyperthermia (39.6 C), tachycardia (148 bpm), hypertension (178/104 mmHg), extensor posturing, and persistent lead-pipe rigidity
Acute rhabdomyolysis (CK 4,850 U/L, myoglobinuria) with acute kidney injury (creatinine 1.4 mg/dL, potassium 5.1 mmol/L)
Administration of haloperidol 5 mg IM x2 in severe TBI with high risk of NMS and impaired neurorecovery
Mental status deterioration (GCS 11 to 9) and lactic acidosis (3.2 mmol/L) requiring ICU transfer

summary: 63-year-old male at 36 hours post-onset of large cerebellar ischemic stroke experiencing rapid neurological decline from GCS 15 to 11 (E2V4M5) with forceful vomiting, right CN VI palsy, bilateral Babinski signs, bradycardia (56 bpm), and hypertension (176/94 mmHg). Repeat head CT reveals enlarging left cerebellar infarction with hemorrhagic transformation, complete fourth ventricle effacement, brainstem shift, and early obstructive hydrocephalus. Intravenous mannitol 1 g/kg has already been administered as bridge therapy; proceed with emergent neurosurgical suboccipital decompressive craniectomy and EVD evaluation.
suggested_differentials: Malignant cerebellar edema with acute obstructive hydrocephalus and brainstem compression
Hemorrhagic transformation of cerebellar infarction
Basilar artery thrombosis
detected_red_flags: Rapid GCS drop from 15 to 11 with new right CN VI palsy and bilateral Babinski signs
Complete fourth ventricle effacement, brainstem displacement, and acute obstructive hydrocephalus on CT
Emerging Cushing physiology (HR drop from 82 to 56 bpm, BP 176/94 mmHg)
Urgent need for neurosurgical decompression due to posterior fossa mass effect

summary: 62-year-old female on respiratory step-down who developed acute pleuritic chest pain, near-syncope, severe hypoxemia (SpO2 84% on room air, 93% on HFNC 50 L/min FiO2 0.70), hypotension (92/58 mmHg), tachycardia (126 bpm), JVD, and lactate 3.8 mmol/L after VTE prophylaxis was omitted for five days. CTPA confirms a large saddle pulmonary embolus with RV/LV ratio 1.4 and septal flattening; hs-troponin I is 412 ng/L and NT-proBNP is 3,840 pg/mL. Initiate immediate systemic anticoagulation, hemodynamic stabilization, and urgent evaluation for systemic IV thrombolysis.
suggested_differentials: Acute high-risk saddle pulmonary embolism with right ventricular failure
Acute coronary syndrome
Cardiac tamponade
detected_red_flags: Severe acute hypoxemia (SpO2 84% on room air requiring HFNC FiO2 0.70) and tachypnea (RR 30 breaths/min)
Obstructive shock physiology (BP 92/58 mmHg, HR 126 bpm, near-syncope, JVD, lactate 3.8 mmol/L)
Large saddle pulmonary embolus with severe RV strain (RV/LV ratio 1.4, troponin I 412 ng/L, NT-proBNP 3,840 pg/mL)

summary: 64-year-old female with AChR-antibody-positive generalized myasthenia gravis in neurorehabilitation developing acute impending myasthenic crisis two days after starting oral ciprofloxacin 500 mg BID alongside daily magnesium oxide 400 mg. Presents with worsening bilateral ptosis, nasal dysarthria, pooled secretions, neck flexor weakness (2/5), orthopnea, single-breath count drop from 32 to 11, FVC 14 mL/kg, and NIF -19 cmH2O. ABG shows rising PaCO2 (46 mmHg, pH 7.36) despite tachypnea (RR 26 breaths/min) and falsely reassuring SpO2 (93%). Requires emergent ICU transfer for early airway protection, immediate discontinuation of ciprofloxacin and magnesium oxide, and initiation of IVIG or plasmapheresis.
suggested_differentials: Impending myasthenic crisis precipitated by fluoroquinolone and magnesium exposure
Cholinergic crisis secondary to pyridostigmine excess
Acute aspiration pneumonitis or early hospital-acquired pneumonia
detected_red_flags: Critical neuromuscular respiratory decline (FVC 14 mL/kg, NIF -19 cmH2O, single-breath count 11) crossing intubation thresholds
Ominous rising PaCO2 (46 mmHg) despite tachypnea (RR 26) and paradoxical supine breathing despite preserved SpO2 (93%)
Severe bulbar dysfunction with secretion pooling and weak cough creating high airway compromise risk
Active exposure to contraindicated agents in myasthenia gravis (ciprofloxacin 500 mg BID and magnesium oxide 400 mg daily)
